author: sjm41
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
PTN000295490 (PTHR12713)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Fly Vha13 (FBgn0283536) and orthologs.

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**
Erroneous source


VACUOLAR ATP SYNTHASE SUBUNIT G (PTHR12713) is annotated with:
ATP hydrolysis activity (GO:0016887)
based on 2 source MGI annotations to Atp6v1g1 (Q9CR51) and Atp6v1g2 (Q9WTT4) from PMID:12133826.

The "V1 domain" (subcomplex) of the V-ATPase comprises 8 subunits (A to H), and is responsible for the ATP hydrolysis activity of the V-ATPase. However, the ATPase activity occurs specifically in the A subunits, whereas the other subunits (including this subunit G) provide regulatory roles or interact with the other ("V0") domain.

See PMID:20450191 for a review.

So can you remove "ATP hydrolysis activity" from PTN000295490 please?
(it already has the MF "proton-transporting ATPase activity, rotational mechanism", so the MF is covered by that. And I see human ATP6V1G1 and ATP6V1G3 also have "ATPase binding" annotated.)


@LiNiMGI   
Table 1 of PMID:12133826 shows the ATPase activity of the whole V-ATPase complex containing either the G1 or G2 subunit, so it's not showing ATP hydrolysis activity specifically of Atp6v1g1 or Atp6v1g2 - so I'd suggest those MGI annotations are removed.
title: PTN000295490 (PTHR12713)

author: marcfeuermann
body:
Thanks for pointing this out. I've removed the annotation. For the past two months, I've been working on the review of families annotated some time ago and I've found a few similar cases of annotation of non-catalytic sub-units with enzymatic activity. An old-fashioned way of doing things, of which there are still traces.
Cheers,
Marc.
